Results.ReviewText:
Overall, I am very happy with this grill.  It will preheat to 550-600 degrees in about 10 minutes.  It does a very good job searing and leaving grill marks on steaks.  On average, it takes about 8 minutes to cook a 1" steak to medium rare.  This will depend alot on the quality of the meat. Caveat:  when you first turn on the propane, give the grill 10 or so seconds before lighting the burners.  If done too soon, the regulator will decrease the gas flow and the grill will not preheat above 250-300 degrees.
My primary complaint is placing a  propane tank on the gravity scale.  I am 70 plus years old with a reverse total shoulder replacement for my right shoulder and I do not have the strength to lift the tank straight up from the ground.  I either do not hook the tank to the scale, or have someone do it for me.  Surely Weber could have done a better design.  I skipped ease of assembly as the grill was assembled by Lowes.

Results.ReviewText:
This is my second Weber grill. Between my first Weber and the one I have now I owned an off brand grill that rusted to the point of being non-functional in 7 years. I went back to Weber for the quality of their grill parts, mainly the stainless steel parts. I  know the cast iron grate and flavor bars will rust over time but stainless steel replacements are available for those parts.
As for the cooking system, the way that grease is routed away for your food is genius. Just enough hits the flavor bars to smoke but not ignite. The grease is routed away and collected in a disposable tray.
The grill heats quickly and can easily reach 500 degrees. Plenty of BTUs on hand.
The only reason I did not give it a 5-star rating is because I have not had it long enough to see how it holds up to weather. I live in Wisconsin and I do not have indoor storage.
So far I love this Grill.

Results.ReviewText:
I need to start to say that my love of Weber all started helping my father use his charcoal Weber grill. As a kids I was amazed at how good the food would taste with that grill and how much my dad loved to use it. I grew and after college I bought my dad the first Weber gas grill. He loved that as well and I bought one as well. My original Genesis lasted me 14 years, only ever replacing the parts that were supposed to wear out. I had a Weber cover that sometimes went on and others it did not. My point is it sat in the elements in the North East and never failed me.  I actually gave it to my neighbor who still uses it. I now wish I kept it.
3 years ago I decided to replace my Weber Genesis for a Spirit E-310 which was a big 's spurge for me. I love the grill, the way it makes the food taste and its performance. Love it until this spring. When I cleaned the grill for spring use the large door came loose and then came off due to rust at the bottom. I used it anyway and it did not affect the performance of the grill. 

I still have the sticker that states a 10 year limited warranty. Weber has always had EXCELLENT customer service so I called. The Weber representative said that the frame was not covered for 10 years, only 2 years. When I bought the grill I would have never thought in a million years that this would totally rust out in 2 years. 
When I discussed the situation the Weber representative they told me I could order a new base for $87.00 shipped. I bought it and tonight tried to install it and unfortunately the rust issue is far worse than I anticipated. There is literally nothing on side or back to attach the new base to. The back and one side are severely rusted. 

So to sum it up-I spent well over $500.00 to buy the new grill 3 years ago. The base side and back have totally rusted out and I have spent $87.00 on a part that cannot be installed to fix the problem. I'm going to call Weber tomorrow to see how much essentially the 3 sides of the grill are to replace it all.

In my entire life with Weber I have never encountered mechanical or rust issues-ever. I cannot explain how disappointed I am over this entire situation. We make a modest living and this grill was a reach and expected more.  I may not ever buy Weber again.
Results.Title: Rust killed grill in 3 years

46510001.Name: Spirit E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
46510001.Description:
Add flavor to the menu with a Spirit E-310. It’s the ideal grill for entertaining a small crowd or a perfect solution to any family meal. Place serving trays and spices on the side tables so that everything you need is where you are, when you need it. With features such as porcelain-enameled, cast-iron cooking grates that retain even heat, you’re guaranteed the best tasting food. It’s built to last with a cookbox that helps prevent rusting and peeling, and conveniently equipped with six tool hooks for easy accessibility of grilling tools. If that wasn’t enough, the low maintenance and easy-to-clean grease management system takes the hassle out of cooking.


• Durable, easy-to-clean porcelain-enamel cast iron grates.

• Porcelain-enameled finish helps prevent rusting and pealing.

• Six tool hooks for easy accessibility of grilling tools.

• Low maintenance and easy-to-clean grease management system.

• 424 square inches of main grilling space.


 This product requires assembly.
